applicant_utility.summary: For the September 2027 start the Faculty of Science has exactly one Amsterdam Merit Scholarship, worth 26,125 EUR, and the university is explicit that it is cash paid in instalments rather than a fee waiver, so you must still budget the full mandatory tuition fee and the institution contribution on top. That makes the award a living-cost subsidy, not a free ticket, and it means the faculty is looking for candidates whose alternatives are constrained by money, not just candidates with the best CV. Because the application needs a motivation letter of at most 500 words plus a CV, treat those two documents as the whole contest: the faculty selects in March and tells you in April, so you will know the outcome well before you have to arrange funds for August.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Ambitious master's applicants, including to the Artificial Intelligence programme in the Faculty of Science, with strong academic records and a genuine funding gap that the award would close.
application_readiness_checklist: Check the Faculty of Science page and the AMS portal for the exact opening date, generally mid-December to mid-January
Write a 500-word motivation letter that covers academic achievement, leadership, motivation and your actual financial situation
Apply for admission to the programme as well, since the scholarship is linked to being accepted for the 2027-2028 intake
Prepare a CV that evidences extracurricular engagement, which is an explicit selection criterion
Check whether you hold, or are applying for, other funding, because the AMS is not combined with other support for the same purpose
Have the full tuition fee and living costs covered from somewhere else, since the award alone will not cover them
common_rejection_risks: Assuming the AMS waives tuition, when the faculty states it cannot be used as a tuition fee waiver
Missing the 15 January Faculty of Science deadline, with no chance to top up an incomplete file later
Leaving the motivation letter over 500 words, which breaks an explicit requirement
Applying for funding for a second year without checking the 40 ECTS first-year condition
Being enrolled in a preparatory or foundation year at a Dutch institution, which makes you ineligible
Counting a commercial student loan as available money, which removes the financial-need criterion
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The full mandatory non-EU tuition fee and institution contribution, plus rent, food, insurance and transport in Amsterdam; the AMS is paid in two instalments in early December and January, so no early payout is available.
document_audit: Start assembling the CV and motivation letter before the portal opens, since December and January are the window
If the programme admission process already gives you an acceptance decision, include it, as the selection runs in March with notifications in April
Keep any evidence of other funding applications separate and clear, since double-funding for the same purpose is excluded
alerts: Only complete applications are considered, so a missing motivation letter or CV ends the application
There is one Faculty of Science award for the 2027-2028 intake, so the odds are a single decision, not a ranking
The Amsterdam Graduate Scholarship and other UvA funds follow their own rules and processes, so do not assume the AMS process applies to them
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Apply to your master's programme, submit the AMS application with the 500-word motivation letter and CV through the portal by 15 January, and track the faculty's selection in March and notification in April.
